overview: The kingdom of Pagan, on the Irrawaddy, united the Burmese lands under Anawrahta in the 1050s and made Theravada Buddhism the faith of the country. Its kings and people covered the plain of Bagan with thousands of temples in two hundred years.

items.text: More than 2,000 temples and stupas still stand at Bagan out of some 10,000 built between the eleventh and thirteenth centuries.
The Ananda temple, finished about 1105 under Kyansittha, with its four standing Buddhas and gilded spire.
Burmese writing, adapted from the Mon script, appears on the Myazedi inscription of 1113 beside Pyu, Mon and Pali.
Anawrahta adopted Theravada Buddhism under the Mon monk Shin Arahan and in 1057 took Thaton, bringing its monks and scriptures to Pagan.
Contacts with Sri Lanka in the twelfth century renewed the monastic ordination and the Pali canon.
Weirs and canals in the Kyaukse district fed the rice that paid for the temples.
Theravada Buddhism remains the religion of most of Myanmar.

fall.text: Mongol armies invaded in 1277 and 1287, and King Narathihapate fled and was murdered by his own son. His successors ruled as Mongol vassals until the three brothers of Myinsaing deposed the last of them in 1297.
